title: Matthew Brown: Amentum hangars at Pax River house anomalous material
place_text: Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland

tellings.quote: Um I think whistleblower Matthew Brown talked about Amentum hangers at at uh at Puxen River housing some anomalous stuff
shouldn't be an issue for you to get a tour of the special project hangers owned by Amentum Core
tellings.difference: Comes straight from Brown's tweet and suggests Musk tour the hangars, without explicitly saying they hold anomalous material.
tellings.link_reason: Both are about Matthew Brown's claim of special Amentum hangars at Pax River.

as_told.title: Tweet: Amentum's special-project hangars at Pax River
as_told.place_text: Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland

tellings.quote: Anyways, next time you are visiting the @WashingtonDCYRs, ask for a tour of @NASPaxRiverPAO! Since you have "all the clearances" it shouldn't be an issue for you to get a tour of the special project hangars owned by @amentum_corp (and other fun spaces). Make sure to look up!

plain: Hangars at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, a Navy base in Maryland, owned by a company called Amentum are said to hold anomalous material. The online researcher UAPGerb tells Michels that the Pentagon whistleblower Matthew Brown said so, and Brown himself reads out his post on X, the social media site, of 6 June 2025, telling the businessman Elon Musk it "shouldn't be an issue for you to get a tour of the special project hangars owned by @amentum_corp (and other fun spaces). Make sure to look up!" The post does not say what the hangars hold; that they house anomalous material is how the tellers read it.

discussion.by: Matthew Brown (@SunOfAbramelin), post on X addressed to Elon Musk
discussion.text: In the post on X of 6 June 2025, Brown asks Musk to request a tour of "the special project hangars owned by @amentum_corp (and other fun spaces)" at Naval Air Station Patuxent River and adds "Make sure to look up!"; the post does not say what the hangars hold, and that they house anomalous material is the tellers' reading of it.
